sarah (Design): Quick accessibility sweep notes from today's compact sidebar QA. found some things that block keyboard and screen reader discoverability.
kevin (Frontend): can you list the blockers?
sarah (Design): 1) the help/shortcuts icon in the sidebar has no visible label on focus (only tooltip on hover). keyboard users can't tell what it does. 2) when opening the shortcuts overlay, VoiceOver doesn't announce the heading. 3) small icon buttons inside the panel are < 32px interactive area.
tia (Accessibility): thanks. a few more details: the overlay is marked role="dialog" but lacks aria-modal and aria-labelledby. NVDA users reported landing in the dialog but not having their virtual cursor move to content. also contrast for the inline keycaps is 3.6:1 on dark backgrounds.
kevin (Frontend): sounds like a mix of semantics and styling. current implementation uses <div role=\"dialog\"> and a visually hidden heading, but maybe ID mapping broke during refactor.
kevin (Frontend): proposed fixes: add aria-modal="true" + aria-labelledby pointing at h3 inside overlay, increase keycap text color token to --keycap-contrast, and add .hit-target to icons: ```css
.icon-btn .hit-target { position: absolute; inset: -6px; border-radius: 6px; }
.button:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }
```
 tia (Accessibility): outline 3px is good for compact controls. ensure color passes 4.5:1 for text under 18pt. for the keycaps we usually aim for 4.5:1 unless bold. also prefer using box-shadow for focus rather than outline to avoid layout shifts in browsers that do not support outline-offset uniformly.
oliver (DevEx): prefer scoped changes and a test harness for the overlay so we can run automated a11y scans on PRs.
sarah (Design): one UX note: when the overlay opens it steals focus from the main list but doesn't trap. users can tab behind the overlay. we should trap focus and restore to the shortcut icon when closed.
tia (Accessibility): yes, use focus trap with aria-hidden for background or inert attribute. also add a keyboard shortcut to close with Escape and announce on close via aria-live polite: "Keyboard shortcuts closed" so screen reader users are aware.
kevin (Frontend): implementation plan: 1) add aria-labelledby + aria-modal + focus trap (PR), 2) increase contrast token for keycaps + update CSS for hit target and focus box-shadow (PR), 3) add sr-only label on the sidebar icon so it reads in the nav, 4) add Playwright e2e to assert focus trap and Axe scan.
a11y-bot: Scan summary for /sidebar/shortcuts: issues flagged - Missing aria-modal (High), Focus not trapped (High), Contrast ratio 3.6:1 (Medium), Interactive hit-area <44px (Medium). See https://ci.example/reports/1850004321.
sarah (Design): can we also avoid adding visible text unless necessary? prefer minimal UI change: keep icon but expose label for assistive tech and show small hover label for mouse users.
tia (Accessibility): add aria-label to the icon ("Keyboard shortcuts") and include a visually-hidden <span> inside the button for redundancy. hover label should be CSS-only so no JS required. ensure it is accessible on focus too.
kevin (Frontend): will scope changes to overlay and sidebar only. question: do we change the global keycap color token or create a variant for compact mode?
oliver (DevEx): create a compact-mode token so we don't unexpectedly affect other components. we can later reconcile in a global token PR if needed.
sarah (Design): timeline? can we target this for the upcoming patch release? low-risk but important for accessibility.
kevin (Frontend): I'll open the first PR today for the semantic fixes + tests. will include Axe baseline.
tia (Accessibility): i'll run manual VoiceOver / NVDA passes once PR is up. please tag me.
a11y-bot: Reminder: file a P2 issue and add label "a11y-fix". Auto-assign to kevin.
sarah (Design): added checklist: 1) PRs for semantics, focus trap, contrast (kevin) 2) Axe + Playwright tests (kevin) 3) manual screen reader pass (tia) 4) compact token created (oliver) 5) ship in patch (oliver).
kevin (Frontend): starting work, I'll drop PR links in this thread when ready.
sarah (Design): thanks team :tada:
